extraction.Name: Philip Marshall
extraction.Cancelled: does not know if patent has been canceled
extraction.Refused/Protested: accepted this patent with protest knowing that taxes would eventually take the land, and that it would have been much better if the patent had lain in trust
extraction.Recorded patent: on the 18th day of August 1921 he had this patent recorded at Martin, South Dakota by Nita Cozad
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold this land in fair consideration in order to meet the second loan
extraction.Buyer: Philip Marshall sold the land to Mr. Bert McAllister of Martin, South Dakota, who undertook to pay the second loan and more taxes amounting to about $1600.00, and that the balance from this sale was about $922.00 of which only $300.00 was paid to him and the balance due him was held by Mr. H. A. Tukey of Omaha, Nebraska, who had the first mortgage on Mr. McAllister's property
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the second loan was made in order to pay the first loan including the interest and taxes on land; sold this land in fair consideration in order to meet the second loan; does not know if tax assessments or tax sales have been canceled, or paid assessments refunded
extraction.NOTES: Patent was mailed like an ordinary letter in December 1919 and not receipted for; received two loans from the land covered by his patent; two loans were redeemed; has the second mortgage on Mr. McAllister, who was foreclosed by a sheriff's sale; states he has been defrauded of his land in the sale; Mr. Oliver Walcott of Valentine, Nebraska is looking after his interest but seems unable to do anything on account of the mortgages; Oliver Walcott of Valentine, Nebraska made the loans; four children depending on him for support; mentally and physically sound but very financially poor; state nor government does not help him; document sworn December 1928; notary commission expires April 20th 1930; County of Lawrence, State of South Dakota
